common_hardware: Nexus 5 (LG)
notes: Tier-4 evidence chip, re-anchored by the Tier-4 audit (docs/verification-tier4.md). The reproducible arbitrary-waveform proof is the MobiSys 2018 'Shadow Wi-Fi' nexmon SDR patch (FULL C source), not the WiSec 2017 jammer previously cited: three ioctls -- 426 NEX_WRITE_TEMPLATE_RAM, 427 START, 428 STOP -- write int16 I/Q into the D11 Template RAM and key the TX chain, emitting an arbitrary baseband buffer (not an 802.11 frame) in 2.4/5 GHz. TX-only; waveform length bounded by Template-RAM depth; band-limited, low-dynamic-range front-end. Monitor/injection/CSI are verified; arbitrary-TX stays 'reported' because the demonstrated target is a rooted Nexus 5 on stock fw 6.0.1 M4B30Z (EoL, hard to source) -- the same primitive on the Raspberry Pi bcm43455c0 is the practical path. The WiSec 2017 reactive jammer is an APPLICATION of this primitive but ships binary-only firmware deliberately restricted to NEXMON/JAMMER MACs, so it is not the reproducible route. Removed the prior 'raw-iq' flag: nexmon exposes frequency-domain CSI, not time-domain IQ receive.

notes: PURPOSE-BUILT radar included as the yardstick, NOT a repurposed Wi-Fi chip. Single-chip FMCW radar: IWR6843 at 60-64 GHz (industrial/IoT), AWR1642/AWR6843 at 76-81 GHz (automotive, band outside this catalog's enum). Full control of the chirp waveform (start freq/slope/ramp) and raw ADC IQ streamed off-chip via DCA1000EVM into mmWave Studio, then range-FFT -> Doppler-FFT -> angle-FFT. Delivers true range-Doppler-angle imaging with ~cm range bins -- tier 4 natively (arbitrary FMCW + raw IQ), documented PHY. This is what the beam-SNR Wi-Fi approach is measured against.

fw_arch: Synopsys ARC (ARCompact) WiGig firmware; MIPS/ARM host running LEDE/OpenWrt

notes: The workhorse of practically all 60 GHz Wi-Fi sensing research: 32-element planar phased array, single 60 GHz stream. Teardowns show Sparrow QCA6320+QCA6310 silicon; sensing papers commonly write 'QCA9500 transceiver' for the same wil6210/ARC family. SEEMOO's LEDE port gives root + custom firmware loading; nexmon-arc's sweep_dump exposes per-sector beam-SNR at /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phyX/wil6210/sweep_dump. Used for device-free localization, gesture recognition, and short-range SAR imaging via aperture motion. Distinct from the already-cataloged qualcomm-qca9500 chip record.
